approved: Defence Legislation (Enhancement of Military Justice) Bill 2015

The Defence Legislation (Enhancement of Military Justice) Bill 2015 was moved for a second reading, introducing amendments to clarify service convictions, create new service offences for assault occasioning actual bodily harm and unauthorised use of a Commonwealth credit card, replace recognisance release orders with non-parole periods, and extend the appointments of the Chief Judge Advocate and full-time judge advocate for two years.

The speaker announced support for the Defence Legislation (Enhancement of Military Justice) Bill 2015, which includes amendments to clarify service convictions, create new service offences, and extend the appointments of the current Chief Judge Advocate and full-time judge advocate. The speaker also thanked former Chief of Army Lieutenant General David Morrison for 36 years of service and praised his leadership on cultural change.

The Defence Legislation (Enhancement of Military Justice) Bill 2015 implements recommendations from over 17 reviews since 1994, creating new service offences for assault occasioning actual bodily harm and unauthorised use of Commonwealth credit cards, and establishing statutory recognition for the Director of Defence Counsel Services to promote independence. The bill also amends the Defence Force Discipline Act to require disclosure of court-martial or Defence Force magistrate convictions as Commonwealth offences, and removes recognisance release orders in favour of non-parole periods for imprisoned service members.

The bill clarifies the legal status of service offences and extends the appointment of the current Chief Judge Advocate and full-time Judge Advocate for two years. It also includes other minor amendments to modernise the military justice system.
